preferred_patterns: Prefer incremental evolution over big-bang rewrites.
Prefer additive API changes when existing consumers must remain stable.
Reuse existing fetch paths, shared components, and validation patterns when practical.
Favor non-blocking background hydration over synchronous page-load fan-out.
Keep rollback steps, validation evidence, and operating notes close to each material change.
discouraged_patterns: Avoid new browser-triggered WG API calls when stored or server-fetched data already exists.
Avoid unbounded polling, queue fan-out, or retry loops.
Avoid large unscoped refactors during feature delivery.
Avoid undocumented payload drift between code, tests, and runbooks.
Avoid changing public payload shape without explicit contract review and regression coverage.
review_priorities: Observable failure modes and validation evidence.
Bounded local and upstream API load.
Consistency with existing battlestats UX and contracts.
pre_commit_requirements: Before every commit, review changed project documentation and update or synthesize the durable docs that describe the new behavior, contract, workflow, or operational state.
When documentation is uncertain or lags reality, check the docs against the live code and tests before committing.
Before every commit, ensure the touched behavior has appropriate automated coverage; add or update focused tests when the current suite no longer proves the changed behavior.
Before every commit, move superseded or historical runbooks out of agents/runbooks/ into agents/runbooks/archive/ so active runbooks remain the current source of truth.
Before every commit that implements changes described in a runbook or spec, update the corresponding runbook to reflect the implementation status, fixes applied, and validation results.

Never state a production configuration value in a doc, a commit message, or an analysis without naming its authority and the date observed. The authority is server/deploy/deploy_to_droplet.sh or the live /etc/battlestats-*.env -- never a code default, never prose in another doc, never inference from data shape. Prefer a pointer ("prod=105, pinned in deploy_to_droplet.sh") over a copied number. When a change touches env-gated behavior, run server/scripts/check_env_drift.sh and resolve checks 1 and 3 before committing.
decision_rules: Prefer the smallest safe vertical slice.
Prefer reversible changes over clever shortcuts.
Validate touched areas with focused tests before widening scope.
Preserve current user-facing behavior unless the task explicitly changes it.
When an endpoint or payload changes, update contract docs and API-facing tests in the same tranche.
Do not commit until documentation review, code-vs-doc reconciliation for uncertainties, appropriate test updates, and runbook archiving have been completed.

Before proposing that a production setting be reduced, reversed, or removed, establish why it holds its current value. A setting sized for a roadmap commitment is not slack to reclaim -- confirm intent against the runbooks and work-items, or ask, before recommending a rollback.
claude_md_rules: CLAUDE.md is always-loaded default context; keep it a thin dispatch file (repo-global defaults + pointers), targeting under ~1,500 words / ~200 lines.
Do not inline environment-variable catalogs in CLAUDE.md; move them to a runbook/reference doc and link it.
Do not inline deep architecture, queue/cache/scheduling internals, or incident history in CLAUDE.md; these belong in agents/runbooks/.
Recurring multi-step workflows belong in .claude/skills/, not as inline procedures in CLAUDE.md.
Prefer a file-path pointer over an embedded explanation whenever one exists. Full re-slim procedure: agents/runbooks/runbook-claude-md-durability.md.

When CLAUDE.md names a live env value, use the authority-carrying form: value, date set, and the file that pins it (see BATTLE_HISTORY_ARCHIVE_RETENTION_DAYS and SHIP_LEADERBOARD_WINDOW_DAYS). A bare number with no authority is the drift pattern that costs debugging time.
